nodes.label: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
nodes.author: Wei Zhou, Xuanhe Zhou, Shaokun Han, Hongming Xu, Guoliang Li, Zhiyu Li, Feiyu Xiong, Fan Wu
nodes.rationale: Systematic experimental study of agent memory from data management perspective, decomposing into four core modules and evaluating 12 representative systems across five benchmark workloads.

nodes.label: Four-Module Memory Framework
nodes.rationale: Decomposition: (1) Memory Representation & Storage (logical + physical), (2) Memory Extraction (input transformation), (3) Memory Retrieval & Routing (query execution), (4) Memory Maintenance (lifecycle governance).

nodes.label: Memory Representation: Token-Level, Graph/Tree, Heterogeneous Composite
nodes.rationale: Three logical representation categories: (1) Token-Level (discrete text or continuous vectors), (2) Graph/Tree-Based Topology (temporal KGs, hierarchical trees), (3) Heterogeneous Composite (multi-part containers).

nodes.label: Memory Storage: In-Context, Single-Engine, Multi-Engine
nodes.rationale: Three physical storage categories: (1) Transient In-Context Registers (KV caches), (2) Specialized Single-Engine (vector DB, graph DB, relational DB), (3) Heterogeneous Multi-Engine (distributed backends).

nodes.label: Memory Extraction: Raw Concatenation, Schema-Free, Schema-Constrained
nodes.rationale: Three extraction strategies: (1) Raw Sequence Concatenation (minimal overhead), (2) Schema-Free Semantic Extraction (free-form text/vectors), (3) Schema-Constrained Structured Extraction (typed triplets/relational payloads).

nodes.label: Memory Retrieval: Attention, Dense, Topological, Agentic, Hybrid
nodes.rationale: Five retrieval categories: (1) Native Attention-Based, (2) Semantic-Based Dense Retrieval (KNN), (3) Topological Subgraph Traversal, (4) Autonomous Agentic Routing (function calls, query expansion), (5) Multi-Stage Hybrid Execution.

nodes.label: Memory Maintenance: Multi-Versioning, Eviction, Consolidation, Optimization
nodes.rationale: Four maintenance strategies: (1) Timestamp-Based Multi-Versioning (append-only logs), (2) Capacity-Driven Physical Eviction (FIFO, score-based), (3) LLM-Driven Semantic Consolidation (inline compaction, tool-driven CRUD), (4) Continuous Parametric Optimization.

nodes.label: Finding 1: Workload-Aligned Memory
nodes.rationale: No single memory architecture dominates all scenarios; effectiveness depends on workload alignment: temporal/graph for cross-session reasoning, summary-first for exact grounding, trace-preserving for stateful execution.

nodes.label: Finding 2: Evidence-Centric Memory Organization
nodes.rationale: Retrieval quality depends on evidence organization for reconstruction rather than top-1 ranking; explicit structure (links, hierarchy) most valuable for scattered/temporally distant evidence.

nodes.label: Finding 3: Temporal Update Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Reliable post-update behavior is pipeline-level design problem; revisability via entity binding, query-time selectivity via filtered routing, LLM scaling for answer refinement.

nodes.label: Finding 4: Horizon-Structured Memory
nodes.rationale: As memory horizon grows, challenge shifts from storage to abstraction choice: multi-view filtering for distractors, relation-aware indexing for distant facts, coarse-to-fine summarization for session-level structure.

nodes.label: Finding 5: Operational Scaling Rule
nodes.rationale: Efficiency governed by maintenance scope not structure alone; localized update/search strongest cost–utility balance; richer organization helps only when upkeep avoids broad recomputation.

nodes.label: 12 Representative Memory Systems Evaluated
nodes.rationale: MemoChat, Mem0, MEM1, MemAgent, MemTree, Zep, Mem0_g, Cognee, LightMem, SimpleMem, MemOS, MemoryOS, A-MEM, Letta—spanning sequential, structural, and hybrid paradigms.

nodes.label: Five Benchmark Workloads
nodes.rationale: LoCoMo (long-conversation QA), LongMemEval (multi-session memory), DB-Bench (procedural execution), LongBench (context-length robustness), MemoryAgentBench (incremental interactions).

nodes.label: LoCoMo: Long-Conversation QA Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Tests episodic, temporal, open-domain memory over multi-turn interactions; reports Exact Match and Answer F1; used for retrieval fidelity and evidence-distance analysis.

nodes.label: LongMemEval: Multi-Session Long-Memory Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates cross-session fact reconnection and temporal reasoning; reports Substring EM, ROUGE-L F1/Recall, LLM Judge Accuracy; tests knowledge update and temporal reasoning robustness.

nodes.label: DB-Bench: Database Operation Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Evaluates procedural execution across database operations; reports Exact Match and Task Success Rate; tests whether memory supports dependent UPDATE/INSERT operations.

nodes.label: LongBench: Controlled Long-Context Difficulty
nodes.rationale: Evaluates context-length robustness across Short/Medium/Long buckets; tests long-horizon memory stability as effective memory horizon increases.

nodes.label: Ablation M1: Memory Representation & Storage
nodes.rationale: Finding 6: High-retention forms best support exact detail recovery; light compression preserves reasoning but weakens exact matching; hierarchy improves access but cannot restore removed content.

nodes.label: Ablation M2: Memory Extraction
nodes.rationale: Finding 7: Coverage-preserving extraction provides stable balance; coarser segmentation helps thread-spanning questions; limited rewriting supports compositional reasoning; storing both user/assistant turns helps clarification.

nodes.label: Ablation M3: Memory Retrieval & Routing
nodes.rationale: Finding 8: Moderate hybrid fusion preferable for semantically related but lexically diverse evidence; lightweight planning effective for constrained lookup; extra reflection adds overhead without benefit.

nodes.label: Ablation M4: Memory Maintenance
nodes.rationale: Finding 9: Conservative consolidation most effective; delayed flushing leaves evidence fragmented; overly coarse summarization obscures sparse but useful cues; raw context best preserves exact phrasing.

nodes.label: Cost-Effectiveness Frontier: Latency vs. Utility Trade-off
nodes.rationale: LightMem and MemTree occupy strongest efficiency frontier; highly structured systems (Cognee, Zep) reach high utility only at 116.5-155.1s latency; localized maintenance more cost-efficient than global reorganization.

nodes.label: Distinction from RAG and Context Engineering
nodes.rationale: Agent memory is persistent, updatable infrastructure governing full lifecycle (representation, storage, retrieval, maintenance), not stateless read-only retrieval or context window curation.

nodes.label: Distinction from Traditional Database Workloads
nodes.rationale: Agent memory differs: (1) semantic rather than predicate-based access, (2) continuous conflicting observations vs. transactional overwrites, (3) heterogeneous access patterns requiring hybrid execution.

hyperedges.label: Memory System Design Space: Four Modules × Multiple Strategies
hyperedges.rationale: The four-module framework with ablation studies reveals a high-dimensional design space where no single architecture dominates; effectiveness depends on workload alignment and careful module composition.
